clue.text: Prisoners narrate a change into stars

parts.note: cons is slang short for convicts, so prisoners
to narrate a story is to tell it

indicators.note: a change into something means these letters are made over into a new order

explanation.surface: Inmates tell a tale about turning into stars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'change' acts on INTO, giving TION at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A named group of stars forming a pattern in the sky is the standard astronomical sense.

clue.text: Varied focus with Tony not on the beat?

indicators.note: varied means altered or mixed up, so the letters of the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A drummer called Tony loses focus and drifts off the beat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Varied' shuffles the nine letters of FOCUS and TONY together.
explanation.definitionFit: Being off the rhythm or beat of the music is the idiomatic meaning of the phrase.

clue.text: To separate, cut outside page

indicators.note: outside says the word for cut goes round the letter for page

parts.note: a slit is a narrow cut

explanation.surface: Instructions for parting something: slice around the page.
explanation.definitionFit: To divide or break apart is the verb sense, a plain synonym for separating.

clue.text: Phantom at festival round half the capital

parts.note: Eid is a Muslim festival
a round shape is the letter O

indicators.note: half the capital keeps only the first three letters of the city's name

parts.note: the capital of the UK is London

explanation.surface: A ghost seen at a festival near half of London.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half' takes LON, the first half of LONDON.
explanation.definitionFit: An apparition or spectre, a literary word from Greek for an image or ghost.

clue.text: The French for the Rock and the clear

parts.note: le is French for the
the Rock is a nickname for Gibraltar, shortened to Gib
French for the again, the opening phrase applying to each the

explanation.surface: A French phrase for Gibraltar, made plain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The French for' applies to both 'the's: LE, then GIB (Gibraltar, called the Rock), then LE again.
explanation.definitionFit: Clear handwriting or print is readable, the plain synonym here.

clue.text: Purist hot tip for academic job

indicators.note: to tip is to upset or overturn, so the letters are tumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: A purist hands on a hot tip about a university post.
explanation.definitionFit: The post of a tutor at a university or college is an academic position.

clue.text: Belted 1 or charged one

parts.note: taken as written
an ion is an electrically charged atom

explanation.surface: Something belted, or something charged.
explanation.walkthrough: 1 is the answer to 1 across, the theme word; this one is famous for the three stars of its belt.
explanation.definitionFit: The hunter figure in the sky is known for the row of three stars forming his belt.

clue.text: Land for use by 25 before English fiddle result

parts.note: 25 across is the star group also called the Plough, the tool used on land

indicators.note: a result is what comes out of fiddling, so the letters of fiddle come out rearranged

explanation.surface: Farmland to be worked by the farmer before some English fiddling.
explanation.walkthrough: 25 across is also called the Plough. 'result' rearranges FIDDLE into DFIELD.
explanation.definitionFit: Earth turned over for sowing is a kind of land, so the phrase is an example of it.

clue.text: First of a 1 for something like half a century

indicators.note: something like means the words sound roughly the same when spoken

parts.note: spoken loosely as 'alf a century', dropping the h

explanation.surface: Something that has lasted about fifty years.
explanation.walkthrough: The brightest star of a constellation is called its alpha, so 'First of a 1' is the star.
explanation.definitionFit: The brightest star in the southern constellation of the centaur is named as its alpha.

clue.text: 1 that laughed

definitions.meaning: the theme word: the lesser dog in the sky, Canis Minor
from the nursery rhyme Hey Diddle Diddle, where the small dog laughed to see such fun

explanation.definitionFit: Canis Minor is Latin for lesser dog, and the rhyme's dog laughed.

clue.text: Finish of a suit is going to demand this fabric

indicators.note: the finish of a word is its final letter

parts.note: will means is going to, and will as a noun is a demand or command

explanation.surface: The finish of a suit is going to need this cloth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Finish of' takes T, the last letter of SUIT.
explanation.definitionFit: A woven cloth with diagonal ridges, a type of textile.

clue.text: Female in group with health problem

indicators.note: in places the letter for female inside the word for group

parts.note: a unit is a group, as in a military unit

explanation.surface: A woman in a team has a health problem.
explanation.definitionFit: Not in good physical shape, so suffering an ailment of health.

clue.text: Complex arrangement of railway in Bath

indicators.note: an arrangement puts the letters into a new order

explanation.surface: A railway layout in the city of Bath is a complicated arrangement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arrangement of' shuffles RLY, IN and BATH. 'Complex' is a noun: a maze-like network.
explanation.definitionFit: A maze or bewildering network, the noun sense of a complex structure.

clue.text: Picture confusion when made by 25

parts.note: to make hay of something is to throw it into confusion
the Great Bear is also called Charles's Wain

explanation.surface: An image of muddle caused by the Great Bear.
explanation.walkthrough: The Hay Wain is Constable's painting. WAIN is from Charles's Wain, another name for the Great Bear (25 across).
explanation.definitionFit: A famous painting by John Constable of a hay cart in a river is meant.

clue.text: Dressing, good and new, in food

indicators.note: in places good and new inside the word for food

parts.note: aliment is nourishment, food

explanation.surface: A salad dressing, good and fresh, in the food.
explanation.walkthrough: Dressing here is military: soldiers dress ranks by lining them up.
explanation.definitionFit: In drill, dressing ranks means putting soldiers in a straight line.

clue.text: Boy keeping article relating to solvent

indicators.note: keeping means holding within, so the boy's name goes round the article

parts.note: Eric is a boy's name
the is the definite article

explanation.surface: A boy holds onto an item about solvents.
explanation.definitionFit: Ether is a classic solvent, so the adjective describes anything pertaining to it.

clue.text: Being prepared to eat — in the case of a fool, outside

parts.note: re means concerning, in the case of

indicators.note: outside says the word for fool goes round the word for eating

parts.note: an ass is a fool
to dine is to eat

explanation.surface: A fool, ready to eat, stands outside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the case of' is the formal sense of re, as in legal or business letters; 'outside' wraps the fool around the eating.
explanation.definitionFit: Readiness is the state of being ready, a noun for preparedness.

clue.text: Talks down the City among hard-line Tories

indicators.note: among puts the City's letters inside the word for hard-liners

parts.note: dries are hard-line Conservatives, from Thatcher-era slang
EC is the postcode for the City of London

explanation.surface: A politician disparages the City among right-wing Tories.
explanation.walkthrough: Dries were the hard-line Conservatives of the 1980s, opposed to the moderate wets.
explanation.definitionFit: To decry is to disparage, to talk something down.

clue.text: Tile on the beach

definitions.meaning: the pebbles found along a beach

explanation.definitionFit: Shingles are wooden roof tiles, and beach pebbles are called shingle.

clue.text: Killer devouring suitable officer

indicators.note: devouring means taking inside, so the killer's name goes round the word for suitable

parts.note: Cain killed his brother Abel in Genesis
apt means suitable

explanation.surface: A murderer eats a fitting officer.
explanation.definitionFit: A rank of officer in the army, or the commander of a ship.

clue.text: Cutlery and where to use it

definitions.meaning: a set of cutlery in its box
a dining hall, where one eats with cutlery

explanation.definitionFit: A canteen of cutlery is a boxed set, and a canteen is a workplace dining room.

clue.text: Lie in hole with one attached

parts.note: a vent is a hole or opening
I is the Roman numeral for one
on means attached, as a light is on

explanation.surface: Lying in a hole with someone attached.
explanation.definitionFit: A lie is a fabrication, something invented.

clue.text: 1 that's bidden man to depart?

parts.note: vir is Latin for man
go means depart

explanation.surface: Someone who has told a man to go away.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads 'VIR, GO': a man (Latin VIR) told to depart, as a maiden might. 1 is the theme, a constellation.
explanation.definitionFit: The constellation of the maiden, one of the zodiac signs.

clue.text: Mate with great power

definitions.meaning: a major world power in Asia

explanation.definitionFit: China plate rhymes with mate in Cockney slang, and the country is a world power.

clue.text: Provide authorised spectator for sovereign?

parts.note: a cat may look at a king, so a cat is allowed to watch a king
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: Arrange for an official watcher for the monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: The proverb 'a cat may look at a king' makes the cat an allowed viewer of a sovereign.
explanation.definitionFit: To cater is to provide food or what is needed.

clue.text: Port left by composer

parts.note: Thomas Arne was the composer of Rule, Britannia!

explanation.surface: A harbour left behind by a composer.
explanation.walkthrough: LARNE is a port in Northern Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: A harbour town in County Antrim, Northern Ireland, so an example of a port.

clue.text: 1 for suitable bird cherishing a time on a river

indicators.note: cherishing means holding close, so the bird goes round the a and time

parts.note: a grebe is a water bird, suited to a river

explanation.surface: A bird fit for a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cherishing' places AT inside GREBE; then A and R follow. 1 is the theme: Ursa Major.
explanation.definitionFit: Ursa Major is Latin for the Great Bear, a constellation of the northern sky.

clue.text: 1's minimal money finds the sailors angry

parts.note: a sou is an old French coin of tiny value
RN is the Royal Navy
cross means angry

explanation.surface: Sailors are angry about a pittance in pay.
explanation.definitionFit: The cross-shaped group of stars seen in southern skies, an emblem of Australia.
